hints: Apply the binomial theorem to expand $(1 + ax)^6$ up to the term in $x^2$.
walkthrough:
Expand $(1 + ax)^6$ in ascending powers of $x$ using the binomial theorem:
$$(1 + ax)^6 = 1 + \binom{6}{1}(ax) + \binom{6}{2}(ax)^2 + \dots = 1 + 6ax + 15a^2x^2$$

hints: Equate to $-3$ to get $5a^2 - 6a + 1 = 0$ and factorise.
walkthrough:
Identify all products that produce an $x^2$ power in $(1 - 3x)(1 + 6ax + 15a^2x^2 + \dots)$:
$$\text{Terms in } x^2 = [1 \times 15a^2x^2] + [(-3x) \times (6ax)] = (15a^2 - 18a)x^2$$

Divide by $3$ and factorise the quadratic equation in $a$:
$$5a^2 - 6a + 1 = 0 \implies (5a - 1)(a - 1) = 0$$
$$a = 1 \quad \text{or} \quad a = \frac{1}{5} = 0.2$$
